# Intent: <short outcome-oriented title>

## Problem

Describe the present problem in the affected person's own terms. Include the
current workflow and concrete evidence that the problem exists. Do not prescribe
an implementation here.

## Affected people

Name the primary user and any other people materially affected. Distinguish the
person experiencing the problem from the buyer, administrator, operator, or
approver when those are different roles.

## Proposed outcome

Describe the observable end state. State what the affected person will be able
to accomplish and how we will recognize that the outcome has been reached.

## Why now

Explain why this problem deserves attention now and what happens if it remains
unsolved.

## Current alternatives

Describe how people solve or work around the problem today, including manual
steps, competing products, and the option of doing nothing.

## Success evidence

List measurable signals and the baseline they will be compared against. Separate
early adoption or workflow signals from later business or operational outcomes.

## Constraints

Record non-negotiable business, legal, safety, privacy, budget, timing,
integration, operational, and accessibility constraints that are already known.

## Boundaries

State what this body of work explicitly does not include. Mention adjacent
problems that must not silently enter scope.

## Existing implementation

Describe what can be learned from the previous implementation: validated user
needs, useful behavior, failures, technical debt, and assumptions that still
need evidence. The old implementation is evidence, not the new specification.

## Open questions

List unresolved questions that could change the outcome, scope, risk, or design.
Every item must eventually be answered, explicitly deferred with an owner, or
declared irrelevant with a reason before this intent can be accepted.

## Acceptance

- Decider: <human product owner>
- Date: pending
- Notes: pending
